WHY CALL

A practical first step after water damage

Water damage is rarely limited to the spot you can see. Moisture can move under flooring, behind baseboards, into wall cavities and through insulation. A good restoration assessment looks beyond standing water and considers the source, affected materials, moisture levels and the safest sequence for drying and cleanup.

01

Stop the source

If it is safe, shut off the water supply and address the active leak. Avoid electrical hazards and do not enter contaminated water.

02

Remove water quickly

Extraction and removal reduce the time materials stay saturated. The right method depends on water depth, material type and contamination.

03

Dry what remains

Air movement, dehumidification and moisture measurement help identify hidden wet areas that ordinary fans may miss.

WHAT A COMPLETE RESPONSE LOOKS LIKE

From the first call to a dry, documented property

A restoration referral is most useful when the conversation starts with facts. Tell the person answering where the property is, what caused the water if you know, whether the source is still active, which rooms are affected and whether anyone has already attempted cleanup. Those details help the independent provider understand the urgency before discussing the next step.

For a typical water event, the work may begin with a safety assessment and source control. Standing water can then be removed using an appropriate extraction method. Once the bulk water is gone, the focus shifts to materials that still hold moisture: flooring assemblies, drywall, cabinetry, insulation, baseboards and other building components. Drying equipment may be positioned based on the moisture map rather than simply placed in the room that looks wet.

Hollywood properties also vary significantly. A coastal condo may require coordination with building management or another unit. A single-family home may have a roof, plumbing, HVAC or appliance source. A commercial property may need a plan that limits downtime. The service page and neighborhood pages on this site are organized to help you identify those differences before you call.

Before you call

  • Know the property address and ZIP.
  • Identify the source if known.
  • Tell the provider whether water is active.
  • Note rooms and materials affected.
  • Mention sewage or other contamination.
  • Ask who performs the work and what credentials they carry.

Good restoration decisions start with the right questions

Ask what the provider found, which materials are affected, what drying method will be used, how progress will be measured and what parts of the property may require repair after drying. Clear answers help you compare options without relying on vague promises or unsupported guarantees.

FAQ

Questions people ask before calling

How quickly should water damage be addressed?

As soon as practical. The longer porous materials remain wet, the greater the chance of secondary damage, odors and microbial growth.

Do you provide the restoration work directly?

No. This website is a referral service. Calls may be connected to independent restoration providers. Confirm licensing, insurance, pricing and scope directly with the provider you choose.

What should I do before help arrives?

If safe, stop the water source, avoid affected electrical areas, keep people and pets away from contaminated water and document visible damage for your records.

Do you cover Hollywood Beach and Hollywood Lakes?

The campaign is designed to serve Hollywood neighborhoods throughout the city. Use the service-area pages or call with the property address for a more precise referral.

What is the difference between extraction and restoration?

Extraction focuses on removing water. Restoration is broader and may include assessment, drying, cleaning, repairs and other steps needed to return affected areas to a usable condition.
